body.title: Embed the pager in the shell
body.summary: In the chat-panel.ts shell create the pager before the registry and hand it the registry; route line(), renderDiff and the approval-card branch through pager.append (no direct scrollTop writes); on session-restored reset the registry keys and the pager, replay rows with absolute keys (firstIndex + i) and end at the bottom; send transcript-page to prepend; stamp live rows with rowIndex and run the trim; wire the bar and scroll to post load-older; settle the provider lock from total. Update, in this same task, the three shell-text pins in chat-panel.test.ts (the replay loop, the appendKeyed key and the setProvLock expression) and any pin on line()'s scroll. Scroll behaviour itself is proven by the pager tests that drive the real registry; this task's own tests are the shell-text pins and the host integration tests still passing. The host still sends the whole transcript.
acceptanceChecks: The shell embeds the pager source; line(), renderDiff and the approval card append through it and no other code sets the terminal's scrollTop
session-restored replays with keys r<firstIndex + i> through the pager's reset; transcript-page goes to prepend; live rows are stamped and trimmed
The provider lock settles from total
The shell is still one nonce'd inline script with no innerHTML outside the guarded markdown path and no remote origin
The three shell-text pins are updated in this task and the whole chat test suite passes at this commit

tests.name: the shell embeds the pager: line() appends through it, session-restored replays with absolute keys through its reset, transcript-page goes to prepend, live rows are stamped and trimmed, and the provider lock settles from total
the shell is still one nonce'd inline script, with no direct scrollTop write outside the pager, no innerHTML outside the guarded markdown path and no remote origin
